clue.text: Rebellious son pouting and refusing to bow

indicators.note: rebellious letters refuse to stay in line, so the words son and pouting are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sulky, defiant boy won't bow to his parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will not stoop stays upright and declines to bend in deference.

clue.text: The chauffeur generally has to drive

indicators.note: the phrase chauffeur generally has, held within its letters, the word wanted

explanation.surface: A chauffeur is usually the one who has to do the driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' signals that the run of letters across 'chauffeur generally' contains the answer; 'drive' is a noun, an inner impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive in the psychological sense is a strong impulse or desire.

clue.text: Best route to take to become an entertainer

indicators.note: the words best route are to be turned into something else, a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Advice on the road that leads to a career in show business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link; 'to become' tells you the letters of BEST ROUTE change into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubrette is a pert maidservant role in comedy or opera, and the actress or singer who plays it.

clue.text: Striking centre-spread that's really over the top

parts.note: workers who are striking are said to be out

indicators.note: the centre of the word spread is its middle pair of letters

explanation.surface: A magazine's middle pages are eye-catching and outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre-spread' looks like the magazine's middle pages, but 'centre' picks RE from the middle of 'spread'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional and bizarre, beyond the bounds of propriety.

clue.text: With coppers about, are likely to put on an act

parts.note: copper coins are pennies, abbreviated P
re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
to tend to do something is to be likely to do it

explanation.surface: When police officers are around, people are apt to put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but here means small change, pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to feign or make believe, acting out something untrue.

clue.text: Relatively favourable

parts.note: read literally, favourable towards one's relatives, describing the practice of giving jobs to family

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean 'fairly', but it means 'to relatives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism shown to kin, so the adjective describes such partiality.

clue.text: A Frenchman is the writer

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a French gentleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from France turns out to be the author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Frenchman' tempts you towards AMI, French for friend, but it is A plus M for Monsieur. Kingsley and Martin Amis are English novelists.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis and his son Martin are both celebrated British novelists.

clue.text: A well-qualified person set up cronies

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, holds a higher degree

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word set is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A graduate establishes a circle of close friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SET into TES, placed after MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mates are pals or close companions, much as cronies are.

clue.text: Skip and diet perhaps early in the year

parts.note: to skip is to leap or spring

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word diet may appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Jumping about and dieting in the first months of the year, a New Year resolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DIET into TIDE. Springtide is an old poetic word for springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Springtide is a literary name for the spring season, the early part of the calendar.

clue.text: A quarter quietly cross, being sound

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
cross means angry, which is irate

explanation.surface: Someone is a bit annoyed, though apparently in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' seems to mean healthy but is the noun: a breathy h-sound in phonetics.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an aspirate is a breathed consonant, the h noise, so it is a speech noise.

clue.text: Spare key given to one of the family

parts.note: G is one of the musical keys
an aunt is a relative, a member of the family

explanation.surface: A duplicate key handed over to a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' seems to be an extra key but is the adjective meaning thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare can describe a lean, bony build, which is what gaunt means.

clue.text: He'd set out formerly to squat in third-rate housing

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the word for third-rate holds or houses the word for squat inside it

parts.note: third-rate means of low quality, poor
to squat is to sit

explanation.surface: A man explains that he once moved into derelict housing as a squatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' here means explain or expound, not depart; POOR houses SIT to give PO-SIT-OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An expositor is one who expounds, setting forth and explaining a subject.

clue.text: The least experienced can appear most colourful

definitions.meaning: green means raw or inexperienced, so the superlative is most naive
superlative of green as a colour, the most verdant

explanation.definitionFit: Green means both naive and verdant, so its superlative covers the rawest novice and the most vivid foliage.

clue.text: Ben is resolved to become a tip-top dramatist

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and worked out afresh, so the letters of Ben is are reordered

explanation.surface: Ben is determined to become a first-class playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' seems to mean determined but rearranges BEN IS; Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, author of A Doll's House, is one of the great Norwegian playwrights.

clue.text: A man airing his intelligence?

parts.note: seems to describe a show-off, but intelligence means news and airing means broadcasting it

explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' in the old sense of information or news.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who reads out the news on radio or television puts information on air.

clue.text: Possibly ten got very cold and drawn

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word ten in another of its possible arrangements

parts.note: iced means frozen, turned very cold

explanation.surface: Ten people became chilled and looked haggard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns TEN into ENT; 'drawn' looks like haggard but means lured.
explanation.definitionFit: To be drawn in is to be attracted or lured, just as one tempted is.

clue.text: Ships where the company is presented with flowers

parts.note: asters are daisy-like garden flowers

explanation.surface: A firm receives a floral tribute at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' can mean rivers in crosswords, but here it is the plain blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Coasters are small vessels trading along the shoreline from port to port.

clue.text: Calling for seafood to be set before a worker

indicators.note: the seafood is placed ahead of the worker in the answer

parts.note: a clam is an edible shellfish
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Asking for a shellfish dish to be served to a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling for' looks like an order in a restaurant; it is the definition, meaning insistent or demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamant means urgently demanding attention, clamorously insistent.

clue.text: A cock bird causing contention in Israel

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a kite is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A rooster stirring up trouble in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The Amalekites were an ancient desert tribe, enemies of the Israelites in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the Amalekites repeatedly fought the Israelites, a constant source of strife.

clue.text: Interview an attendant when there's evidence of a leak

parts.note: to see someone can mean to interview or meet them
a page is a young attendant or servant

explanation.surface: A job interview for a servant uncovers a security leak.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid that has oozed out, the telltale trace of a slow escape.

clue.text: Shingle may be used in this country

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of shingle could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Pebbles from the beach might serve as a building material here.
explanation.walkthrough: Shingle is beach pebbles or roof tiles; the definition points to the language spoken in this land.
explanation.definitionFit: The national tongue of England is the language spoken across the country.

clue.text: Be paid maybe about fifty for a black-and-white one

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, or around, the letter for fifty
maybe suggests the words be paid in a possible rearrangement

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Getting paid around fifty for a pied horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges BE PAID; 'about' puts PIEBAD around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald horse has irregular patches of two colours, typically dark and pale.

clue.text: Scientist behind Parisian street uprising

parts.note: behind means past, as in behind schedule or past the house

indicators.note: uprising in a down entry means the word for street is read upwards

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A researcher was behind a revolt in the streets of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' suggests revolution but reverses RUE to EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist who pioneered pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: A number might well get involved in a row

definitions.meaning: one of the integers, the figure after seven

definitions.text: might well get involved in a row
definitions.meaning: a rowing crew of oarsmen pulls together in a boat

explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a numeral and also the name of a rowing crew of that many oarsmen.

clue.text: Arrange equipment

definitions.meaning: to organise or set up an event
outfit or kit, a set of clothes or gear

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means organise; as a noun it means an outfit or costume.

clue.text: To keep a check on careless talk?

definitions.text: To keep a check on careless talk?

parts.words: To keep a check on careless talk?
parts.note: sounds like wartime censorship, but gas is idle chatter and the device measures fuel

explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' is slang for idle chatter; the joke has a household meter monitoring it.
explanation.definitionFit: The domestic device records how much fuel a house consumes.

clue.text: The woman should be otherwise engaged about one

indicators.note: engaged about means the word for otherwise is wrapped around the letter for one

parts.note: else means otherwise
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: She ought to be busy with something else around one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's given name, so it can stand for some female.

clue.text: Little supporters running water

definitions.meaning: small pegs that hold up golf balls
a river, the ... in north-east England

explanation.definitionFit: Golfers rest balls on small pegs; the Tees is a river in north-east England.

clue.text: Judge put off by an explosive device

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a mine is a buried explosive

explanation.surface: A magistrate was discouraged by a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a matter is to decide or settle it.

clue.text: Boorish guys are successful in the south-east

indicators.note: the word for success sits in the abbreviation for south-east

parts.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east
to win is to be successful

explanation.surface: Rough men are thriving in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine is an insult for coarse, contemptible people.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader liable to get lost in thought

indicators.note: the leader of revolutionary is its opening letter

parts.note: apt means liable or inclined to

explanation.surface: A rebel chief prone to daydreaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means wholly absorbed or engrossed.

clue.text: Don't order so much, even though it's free

definitions.meaning: read as two words: give fewer orders, charge meaning command

explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' means command in the first reading and price in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Charge means both a command and a fee, so something without charge costs nothing.
